name: Vitamin K2 (MK-7)
summary: Vitamin K2 (menaquinone-7) is the long-acting K2 form positioned for arterial and bone health via matrix Gla protein activation. RCTs include VitaK-CAC (n=180 coronary artery disease patients, less calcification progression over 2 years) and Knapen (n=244 postmenopausal women, reduced arterial stiffness over 3 years). Marketing routinely omits the warfarin interaction.
description: Canonical vitamin K2 research entity for evidence and safety integration. Publication remains held until the warfarin/anticoagulant interaction is prominently documented, MK-4 vs MK-7 form boundaries are explicit, and dose standardization has passed the site's review gates.
primary_effects_or_targets: matrix Gla protein activation; vascular calcification; bone mineralization
